title: Authentication
text: Authentication verifies the identity of a user. Common methods include passwords, multi-factor authentication, and biometric verification.

title: Authorization
text: Authorization determines which resources and actions an authenticated user is permitted to access. Role-based access control is a common approach.

title: SQL Indexes
text: Database indexes improve the speed of data retrieval. They reduce the need for full table scans but require additional storage and can slow down writes.

title: Caching
text: Caching stores frequently requested data in a faster storage layer. Redis is commonly used to reduce database load and improve application response times.

title: Password Security
text: Passwords should be stored using secure password hashing algorithms such as Argon2 or bcrypt, with unique salts. Plaintext password storage should be avoided.

title: REST APIs
text: REST APIs expose resources over HTTP using methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE. They commonly exchange data in JSON format.

title: Asynchronous Processing
text: Background task queues allow slow operations to run outside the request-response cycle. Celery and Redis can process tasks such as sending emails and generating reports.

title: Vector Embeddings
text: Embedding models convert text into numerical vectors that represent semantic information. Similar meanings can produce nearby vectors in an embedding space.

title: Semantic Search
text: Semantic search retrieves information according to the meaning of a query rather than relying only on exact keyword matches.

title: Rate Limiting
text: Rate limiting restricts how many requests a client can make during a time window. It helps protect APIs from abuse and excessive traffic.
